issue: dry_run bullet, /mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/core.py:63-64 — "- ``dry_run`` — validate only: print the preflight report and plan / and return, reading and writing nothing." The "reading ... nothing" half is false. dry_run returns run_preflight(settings, 'mask'), whose describe_plan() calls _inventory() per src (spacr/validate.py:1443 -> :458), which does os.path.exists/isdir/isfile, os.listdir via _listdir (:334), np.load(..., mmap_mode='r') on up to three .npy files in merged/ and stack/ via _peek_planes (:355-377), and _scan_raw_images (:396) listing src, src/orig and src/consolidated. validate_settings additionally stats model/file paths (:1041, :1067, :1129, :1142). Empirically confirmed: run_preflight against a temp dir holding 5 Yokogawa-named .tif files printed "inputs found   5 raw image files" and "channels       1 (01)" — facts obtainable only by reading the directory. The preflight's own printed line is carefully worded "Nothing has been written and no model has been loaded"; the docstring overstated it into "reading and writing nothing".

collect_report — ":returns: ... each inserted after the core section it names". The anchor is NOT restricted to core sections. At /mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/report.py:1816-1822 the lookup `next((index + 1 for index, section in enumerate(sections) if section.key == contribution.after), len(sections))` scans the whole `sections` list, which already contains plugin sections inserted earlier in the same loop (`sections.insert(insert_at, plugin_section)` then `existing_keys.add(...)`). A plugin whose `after` names another plugin's key is inserted after that non-core section. Verified by execution: contributions (plug_a, after='statistics') and (plug_b, after='plug_a') produced ['run_status','provenance','segmentation_qc','plate_qc','figures','statistics','plug_a','plug_b','settings','appendix'] — plug_b's anchor is plug_a, not a core section. The word "core" is a new over-narrow claim of the same species as the defect being fixed, and it contradicts the sibling contract in /mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/plugins.py:165-166, which correctly says "key of the existing section this one is inserted directly after".

save_figure (/mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/timelapse.py:1637): "format, so the file on disk is often ``figure_1.png``." -- the default is the opposite. plot.py:43 sets DEFAULT_FIGURE_FORMAT = "pdf" and qt/preferences.py:229 sets DEFAULT_FIG_FORMAT = "pdf", and figure_output_preferences() falls back to that on any failure, so with no user preference set the file on disk is figure_1.pdf -- the exact extension the rewritten summary line just stopped promising. PNG only appears if the user explicitly selected it in the Qt preference. The rest of that paragraph (extension is a proposal; spacr.plot.save_figure rewrites it via _with_extension) is true.

analyze_calcium_oscillations (/mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/timelapse.py:1846): "writes ... tables to CSV beside the database" -- save_results_dataframe (timelapse.py:1651) writes to os.path.join(os.path.dirname(src), 'results'), i.e. a results/ subfolder of the database's directory, not alongside the .db file. A reader following this looks in the wrong directory.

Run.record_model: "A failure is appended to ``provenance_warnings`` (so it reaches ``manifest.json``) and logged" -- false for every file-level failure. hash_file() catches Exception and returns None (line ~221), and _file_record() catches OSError and returns None (line ~452), so a missing, permission-denied, or directory checkpoint never raises out of the try block and the except handler that appends to provenance_warnings is never reached. Verified empirically by importing spacr.run_journal and calling record_model with (a) a nonexistent path, (b) a chmod-000 file, (c) a directory: all three gave model_hashes: {} and provenance_warnings: [] -- only LOG.warning fired. The handler only fires for exceptions raised outside those two helpers, e.g. Path(checkpoint_path) on a non-path-like object or p.resolve() failing. The deleted sentence ("Silently no-ops if the file is unreadable") was the accurate description of that path, so this replaced a near-true statement with a false one and also dropped the true fact that an unreadable checkpoint leaves NO entry in model_hashes.

hash_file: the new summary "Return the first 16 hex characters of a file's SHA-256, or ``None``." is stated unconditionally and is false on the supported ``full=True`` path, which returns all 64 chars and is the path actually used internally (_file_record line 444, _write_manifest line 724). The claim itself concedes this by saying "on the default path", but the docstring summary does not -- and the summary is what autodoc/tooltips render alone. The :param full: entry two lines below is the only correction. Needs "By default ..." or "(all 64 with ``full=True``)" in the summary line.

generate_training_dataset :param settings: bullet — `- ``tables``: object tables available to the merge helper.` (/mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/io.py:5779). generate_training_dataset never calls a merge helper. `_read_and_merge_data` (io.py:3511) is the merge helper and is not reached from this function; the crop list comes from `_read_db(db_loc=db_path, tables=['png_list'])`, or from `crop_rows_from_object_table(db_path, object_type)` where `object_type` comes from `crop_object_type(png_type)`, not from `tables`. The only real effect of `tables` here is `if 'nucleus' not in tables: settings['nuclei_limit'] = False` / `if 'pathogen' not in tables: settings['pathogen_limit'] = 0`, and those two keys are then dead in this call path (they are not in CROP_SHAPE_KEYS, so `_crop_shape_overrides` does not forward them to `open_crop_source`; deep_spacr.py:3478 goes on to `train_test_model`, which reads image folders). The bullet reproduces the stale in-code comment `# Limits for merge helper` and will read to a user as 'this selects which object tables the crop list is built from', which is false.

AppContribution :ivar screen_factory: "it is passed ``app_key`` and ``host`` if it declares them." -- the plugin screen-factory path in /mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/qt/app.py:2480 calls `screen = factory(app_key=key)` unconditionally: `app_key` is always passed (a zero-arg factory raises TypeError), and `host` is never passed at all. The signature-inspecting "take what you need" contract (`_call_screen_factory`, spacr/qt/app.py:640, which does supply `app_key`/`host` only when declared) is reached at line 2492 for *registered built-in* factories, on the branch after the plugin branch has already returned. The project's own SDK doc contradicts the new sentence too: docs/source/plugin_sdk.rst:81 says "The callable is invoked as ``factory(app_key=...)``".

/mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/batch_correction.py:833-835 — "a caller using ``batch_correction=\"combat\"`` must pass those two alongside this mapping or :func:`correct_from_metadata` raises." FALSE for batch_combat_mean_only. That parameter is `batch_combat_mean_only: bool = False` (line 724) and is never required; the only combat guard (lines 563-576 in correct_batch_effects) raises solely on `covariate is None`. Empirically: correct_from_metadata(feat, meta, batch_covariate_column='cond', **correction_kwargs({'batch_correction':'combat'})) SUCCEEDS with no raise, while omitting batch_covariate_column raises regardless of whether batch_combat_mean_only is passed. The docstring asserts a two-key requirement the code does not impose — exactly one key (batch_covariate_column) is mandatory.

/mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/batch_correction.py:838-839 (lesser) — ":param default_control_column: control column used when ``batch_control_column`` is absent or blank." The code tests `if control_column in (None, "")` — a whitespace-only string such as "  " is NOT treated as blank and is emitted verbatim. The very next :param uses the identical phrase "absent or blank" for default_control_values, where the code DOES strip (`isinstance(control_values, str) and not control_values.strip()`). Identical wording papers over a real asymmetry between the two branches; the control_column line is wrong for whitespace-only input.

evaluate_predictions: "a ``raw_prob_<class>`` / ``prob_<class>`` pair per class" is inaccurate for any class name containing characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_.-]. The code does not use the class name; it builds a sanitized, de-duplicated `safe_name` (re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+', '_', name).strip('_') or f'class_{index}', then a `_2`, `_3`, ... suffix on collision) and names the columns f'raw_prob_{safe_name}' / f'prob_{safe_name}'. Runtime counterexample: classes=['wild type','ko-2','ctrl'] produces columns 'raw_prob_wild_type'/'prob_wild_type', not 'raw_prob_wild type'. The docstring documents the `probability_column_names` summary key (which is exactly this safe-name list) but never ties it to the column suffixes, so a reader following `<class>` literally looks for a column that does not exist.

measure_crop, /mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/measure.py:2673 — new settings-key bullet `- ``dry_run`` — validate the settings and stop; nothing is read, written or imported.` The dry_run branch DOES read and DOES import; only "written" is true. Proven by running measure_crop({'src': <tmp>/plate, 'dry_run': True, 'timelapse': False}): it opened merged/field1.npy six times, listed merged/, plate/, plate/orig and plate/consolidated, and imported spacr.validate, spacr.plugins, spacr.training_basis and difflib during the call. Mechanism: `return run_preflight(settings,'measure')` -> describe_plan -> _inventory (spacr/validate.py:462-503) which calls os.path.exists/isdir, _listdir and _peek_planes (spacr/validate.py:355-378), the latter doing `import numpy as np` and `np.load(..., mmap_mode='r')` on up to three .npy files. The code comment the agent generalised from says only that the HEAVY imports (.io/.timelapse) and the _save_settings_to_db WRITE are skipped — not that nothing is read or imported.

/mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/spacrops.py:141 (spacrStitcher, inside claimed fix #1) — ':param outdir: output folder, created on construction and used for QC images, CSVs and the default feature cache.' The 'CSVs' clause is not true of the code. Every use of self.outdir in spacrStitcher is: os.makedirs (260), the feat_cache default (299), the QC outline PNG (945), the stitched full TIFF/PNG (1003-1004), and score_sorted_line.png (1377). No CSV is ever written under self.outdir. run_folder's csv_path is a required caller-supplied positional argument (1199), and the only real caller, stitch_cycle_wells, deliberately points them at different folders: outdir=qc_pairs_dir (3042) while pairwise_csv goes to results_outdir (3004). A newly added statement that carries a verification stamp but is not backed by the body.

train_model :returns: — "the best checkpoint (the last one written if no epoch was flagged best)". The fallback it paraphrases (`final_path = best_model_path if best_model_path is not None else model_path`, /mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/deep_spacr.py:2677) can never hand back a non-None `model_path`: the in-loop `elif model_path is not None and best_model_path is None: best_model_path = model_path` (line ~2641) fills `best_model_path` in the same iteration `model_path` first becomes non-None, so `best_model_path is None` at return implies `model_path is None` too. The one reachable "no epoch flagged best" case is a resume run (`best_model_path = os.path.abspath(resume_checkpoint)`, line ~2439) where no epoch beats the restored `best_metric`; there the function returns the RESUME checkpoint, not the last file written (`_save_model` does write a `_last_` artifact at `epoch == epochs`). So the parenthetical is false in the only case it purports to describe. Everything else in that :returns: — the `(model, model_path)` tuple and the `(None, None)` on an unbuildable `model_type` — is correct.

choose_model :param height: "nominal input size; used for both dimensions of the square forward sanity check (falls back to ``224`` when falsy)" -- true as far as it goes but materially incomplete, and misleading in context. height is also forwarded as TorchModel(image_size=img_size), where _infer_feature_dim() (utils.py:3869-3886) forwards a (1,3,s,s) dummy at s=image_size and returns out.size(1) as num_ftrs, which sizes nn.Linear(num_ftrs, num_classes) (utils.py:3798-3803). So height changes the model that gets built, not just a throwaway check -- the code comment directly above img_size even says 'infer the right feature dim + pass the sanity check', and the agent kept only the second half. Sitting in a block where channels/width/chan_dict/device are each labelled 'unused', the 'used for <the sanity check>' phrasing reads as exhaustive and tells a caller height is cosmetic.

plot_image_mask_overlay_magenta_outlines (/mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/plot.py:618-621): "Variant of :func:`plot_image_mask_overlay` ... and the masks are read from the last stack planes in pathogen, nucleus, cell order." — the sentence is literally true of this function, but it sits inside the 'here is how the variant differs' clause and the report claims it as one of 'the differences'. The plane mapping is IDENTICAL in the two functions. plot_image_mask_overlay computes base_image_planes = stack.shape[2] - n_masks and assigns cell/nucleus/pathogen/organelle forward from there; the magenta variant assigns pathogen=-1, nucleus=-2/-1, cell=-3/-2/-1. I enumerated all 7 non-empty cell/nucleus/pathogen combinations: every one maps to the same planes. A reader comparing the two docstrings will conclude the plane layout differs when it does not.

plot_image_mask_overlay_magenta_outlines (/mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/plot.py:619-620): "when ``all_on_all`` is False the mask belonging to a channel is drawn in magenta rather than in that object's colour" is only true for mode='outlines' (the '#FF00FF' literal at line ~767). When mode is anything else, that same branch overlays a random-colour filled label via random_color_cmap — identical in kind to plot_image_mask_overlay. The paragraph carries no mode qualifier; only the later :param mode: entry hints at it. Lower severity than the item above (mode defaults to 'outlines'), but it is stated unconditionally.
